raw_response:
I farm this 10.1 mu the same wheat-maize rotation as most people here. I have done it many years, so I mainly follow what has worked on my own land and what the other old farmers nearby do. My family only has 2 people, so I cannot make the management too troublesome, and I also cannot spend too much cash at one time. Wheat still needs to hold the yield, because if wheat is weak, the whole year feels tight. Maize comes right after wheat, so the time is short. I will keep the full 10.1 mu in wheat and then full 10.1 mu in summer maize after harvest. For fertilizer, I would rather not cut too much, because if the crop turns yellow and thin, then saving a little money on fertilizer loses more grain. But I also will not push too high, because pumping water and buying fertilizer both cost money. With well water, I will irrigate when the crop really needs it, mainly wheat more, maize less, unless summer is too dry.
